sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Lophira alata is a large deciduous tree of humid tropical African forests, reaching about 60 m tall. Its trunk can be up to 1.6 m in diameter, exceptionally more.

sections.title: Leaves and flowers
sections.text: The simple, leathery leaves are usually 8–24 cm long and can reach 35 cm. Fragrant white flowers are grouped in panicles.

sections.title: Fruit and uses
sections.text: The conical, woody nut, about 2.5–3 cm long, contains one seed and is accompanied by two unequal, wing-like sepals. The tree is mainly harvested for its dense timber; the sources consulted do not establish a food use.
